Question Choices: Seven different books are placed in three labeled display spots. How many displays are possible? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
Hints: The display spots are distinct, so order matters;Use three descending factors starting at 7
Solution: The three spots are ordered, so $P(7,3)=7\cdot6\cdot5=210$.

Hints: The two roles are different;Choose the captain and then the assistant
Solution: There are 10 choices for captain and 9 remaining choices for assistant.;Thus $P(10,2)=10\cdot9=90$.

Question Choices: The ordered count P(12,5) counts each unordered group of five objects how many times?
Hints: The same five objects can be placed in five ordered positions;Count the orders of 5 objects
Solution: Each five-object group has $5!=120$ orders.;Therefore it is counted 120 times.

Question Choices: A 4-person committee is selected from 10 students. How many committees are possible? Input C(... ...) and P(... ...) for combination and permutation.
Hints: A committee is unordered;Count ordered selections and divide by 4!
Solution: There are $P(10,4)=5040$ ordered selections.;Dividing by $4!=24$ gives $C(10,4)=210$ committees.
